solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tango to repeat incorporating new music genre (6)

indicators.note: ECHO takes N into its body

blocks.note: T = tango in the NATO alphabet
an echo repeats a sound
N = new, placed inside ECHO: ECH(N)O

annotation.surface: A dancer is told to repeat the tango, working in some new kind of music.
annotation.walkthrough: Tango sits beside music genre and pretends to be a dance, but here it is only the letter T.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: techno, the electronic dance music born in Detroit, is one genre among many.

entries.clue: Bishop leaving after some delay in ecstasy (8)

indicators.note: B goes away from the word, leaving the rest

blocks.note: belatedly = after some delay
B = bishop, the chess abbreviation; taken out of BELATEDLY

annotation.surface: A bishop who was held up leaves in a state of rapture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In ecstasy' reads as the bishop's mood; it is the definition, an adverbial phrase matching ELATEDLY.
annotation.definitionFit: To act elatedly is to act in ecstasy, full of joy.

entries.clue: Public building due to be consecrated (8)

blocks.note: a town hall, a public building
due = owed, as a debt

annotation.surface: A civic building is scheduled for its consecration ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Due to be' reads as one phrase meaning scheduled; the split is after 'due', with 'to be' only linking.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hallow is to make holy, as in 'hallowed be thy name', and a church's ground is hallowed when blessed.

entries.clue: Woman with issue failing to start knowing differently (9)

indicators.note: the first letter of MOTHER is dropped

blocks.note: a woman with issue (children) is a MOTHER; without its first letter, OTHER
knowing = wise

annotation.surface: A woman with a problem can't get going and would rather know things another way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' here is the legal word for offspring, not a problem; a woman with issue is a mother.
annotation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in a different way, differently.

entries.clue: Feature of geometry exercise books: endless suffering! (8)

indicators.note: AGONY loses its last letter

blocks.note: PE = physical education, school exercise
NT = New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
AGONY = suffering, without its end

annotation.surface: A pupil groans that geometry exercise books are nothing but misery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exercise books' reads as school jotters, but it splits in two, and 'books' is the usual crossword shorthand for a Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: A pentagon, a five-sided figure, is one of the shapes studied in geometry.

entries.clue: Play in Greek concert and cut number headed for America (10,5)

indicators.note: ETHER is trimmed of its last letter

blocks.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
a 'number' is something that numbs: ETHER, the old anaesthetic, cut short
US-bound = heading for America

annotation.surface: A Greek play and a concert are cut down to size before touring the States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' is the classic crossword trick: read it as numb-er, a thing that numbs, i.e. an anaesthetic.
annotation.definitionFit: Prometheus Bound is an ancient Greek tragedy, traditionally attributed to Aeschylus.

entries.clue: Cry from the heart of ambitious worker, known to be social climber (7)

indicators.note: take the central letter of AMBITIOUS

blocks.note: T is the fifth of AMBITIOUS's nine letters
the ant is a worker known to be social
ivy is a climbing plant

annotation.surface: An ambitious employee, a would-be social climber, lets out a heartfelt cry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social climber' looks like one phrase for a snob; the split is 'social' with the ant and 'climber' alone for IVY.
annotation.definitionFit: Tantivy is an old hunting cry, called when the hounds are at full gallop.

entries.clue: Method for supporting merchandise gets approving comment (4,4)

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the one above, so HOW goes under GOODS

blocks.note: goods = merchandise
how = method, the way something is done

annotation.surface: A new merchandising technique wins a word of praise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Method for supporting merchandise' reads as a display technique; in a down entry 'supporting' means sitting underneath, so HOW goes below GOODS.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Good show!' is an old-fashioned British expression of approval.

entries.clue: Counts maybe on rising talent, dispatching article (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, ON read upwards becomes NO
the article A is sent away from ABILITY

blocks.note: ON turned upwards
ABILITY = talent, minus the article A

annotation.surface: A talent scout counts on rising stars while cutting a news story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counts' looks like a verb; it is the plural of count, the European nobleman, and 'maybe' marks them as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Counts are titled aristocrats, members of the nobility.

entries.clue: Fuss I disapprove of that detains colleague hours (8)

indicators.note: BOO holds ALLY and H inside it

blocks.note: 'boo!' is a cry of disapproval
an ally is a colleague on your side
H = hours

annotation.surface: Someone complains about the fuss when a co-worker is kept back for hours.
annotation.walkthrough: A whole sentence, 'I disapprove of that', stands for a single interjection, and 'detains' then works on it as if it were a jailer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly American in flavour: ballyhoo was the barker's patter outside a circus sideshow, hence any noisy fuss.

entries.clue: After change of tone doctor shut up finally (6)

indicators.note: the letters of TONE are rearranged

blocks.note: TONE rearranged
MB = Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

annotation.surface: After changing his manner, the doctor finally went quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like the doctor falling silent; 'shut up finally' is the definition, to enclose for the last time.
annotation.definitionFit: To entomb is to shut someone up in a tomb, finally and for good.

entries.clue: Help Bill to leave Cheltenham? (8)

indicators.note: Bill leaving Cheltenham means the letters for Bill walk out of the word for Cheltenham

blocks.note: Cheltenham, in England, is a famous racecourse; the ? flags an example
AC = account, a bill; removed from RACECOURSE

annotation.surface: Someone asks for help getting Bill out of Cheltenham.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; it is an account, AC. Cheltenham hosts Britain's big jump-racing festival.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having recourse to something means turning to it for help when other means fail.

entries.clue: Gives out tips on economical fuel (6)

indicators.note: the two tips of ECONOMICAL, its first and last letters

blocks.note: gives out = dies, as an engine does
E and L, the ends of ECONOMICAL

annotation.surface: A leaflet hands out advice on fuel-saving motoring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gives out tips' reads as offering advice; 'gives out' is dies, and 'tips' are letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Named after its inventor Rudolf Diesel, diesel is the heavy oil burned in compression-ignition engines, so a fuel by example.

entries.clue: After reflecting hard, tweet some sudden revelation (8)

indicators.note: H + PIPE is mirrored, and ANY comes after it

blocks.note: H = hard, and to pipe is to tweet like a bird
any = some

annotation.surface: After thinking hard, someone posts a tweet about a sudden insight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' suggests social media; here it is the bird's call, PIPE.
annotation.definitionFit: From the Greek for 'manifestation', first of Christ to the Magi; the everyday sense is a flash of understanding, a close synonym.

entries.clue: Confounded, as men mean to do some shopping! (4,5)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into confusion

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Exasperated at the idea that men intend to go shopping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shopping' is the British slang for informing on someone to the police, not a trip to the shops.
annotation.definitionFit: To name names is to identify wrongdoers, which is to shop them.

entries.clue: Blamed by the head, ultimately that’s not, naturally, fair? (4)

indicators.note: take the last letter of each word

blocks.note: the last letters of blameD bY thE heaD

annotation.surface: A pupil blamed by the head teacher protests that it isn't fair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as just; it means blonde, and hair that is fair but not naturally so has been dyed.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: 'fair' here means blonde, and colour from a bottle is the kind that does not come naturally.

entries.clue: America’s brief: one in Italian outfit would be more fastidious (8)

indicators.note: 'one in Italian outfit' is read literally: the one sits in the team, placed within its letters

blocks.note: a DA, district attorney, is a US lawyer; a brief is slang for a lawyer
I = one, the Roman numeral
Inter Milan, the Italian football club; I goes inside: INT(I)ER

annotation.surface: An American in an Italian suit would look more particular.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, the lawyer. 'Outfit' is a team, not clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: Dainty can mean fastidious or fussy, so daintier is more fastidious.

entries.clue: Making use of our language, not for good (8)

blocks.note: ENG = English, 'our' language for a British setter
agin is dialect for against, i.e. not for
G = good

annotation.surface: Using our language, but not permanently.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not for good' reads as not permanently; it splits into 'not for' (AGIN, against) and 'good' (G).
annotation.definitionFit: Engaging workers is making use of them, hiring their services.

entries.clue: Influence for one needing to carry weight (4)

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within you, so the first word holds the weight inside

blocks.note: say = for one, for example
W = weight

annotation.surface: Having influence means being someone who carries weight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' sounds like 'for a person'; it is 'for example', SAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hold sway over people is to have influence over them.

entries.clue: Fixer on flight from Rio darts out to lunch (5,3)

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters go haywire

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone on a flight from Rio dashes off for lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is a flight of stairs, not a plane trip; a stair rod holds the carpet to each step.
annotation.definitionFit: A stair rod fixes a stair carpet in place on a flight of stairs.

entries.clue: Consent to keep giving separately, and only half, to cause distress (8)

indicators.note: AGREE holds the other letters
the letters go in one at a time, at different places
just the first half of GIVING is used

blocks.note: agree = consent
only half of GIVING's six letters, the first three

annotation.surface: Agreeing to keep donating piecemeal, and only half as much, is bound to upset people.
annotation.walkthrough: An unusual container: 'separately' means G, I and V go in one at a time, AG(G)R(I)E(V)E, not as a block.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though a formal one: to aggrieve is to wrong someone so they feel hurt, familiar mostly from 'aggrieved'.

entries.clue: Table again starts to inconvenience residents and must be moved (8)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the next two words
the letters are shifted about

blocks.note: first letters of Inconvenience and Residents
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A table has to be moved again, starting to bother the residents.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Table' looks like furniture to be moved; in meetings, to table a motion is to submit it.
annotation.definitionFit: To table something again is to put it forward once more: to resubmit.

entries.clue: Difficulty with image that can’t be gone back over (7)

definitions.text: that can’t be gone back over

blocks.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
an icon is an image

annotation.surface: A problem with a picture that can't be retouched.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: the Rubicon is the river Caesar crossed, and a point of no return.
annotation.definitionFit: To cross the Rubicon is to pass a point from which you cannot go back.

entries.clue: Observe Yankee grabbing attention not far away (6)

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so the first piece clasps the next one inside it

blocks.note: NB = nota bene, 'note well'
to give someone your ear is to pay attention
Y = Yankee in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Watch an American grabbing the limelight close by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Observe' is the imperative behind NB, the Latin 'note well' printed in the margins of documents.
annotation.definitionFit: Nearby means close at hand, not far away.

entries.clue: Musicians attempt to have one arrested for piracy? (8)

indicators.note: TRY holds I inside it, as police hold a suspect

blocks.note: a band of musicians
try = attempt
I = one; held inside TRY at its start: (I)TRY

annotation.surface: A group of musicians tries to get one of their number arrested for pirating music.
annotation.walkthrough: The ? marks piracy as one example of banditry, robbery on the high seas.
annotation.definitionFit: Piracy is a kind of banditry, lawless robbery.

entries.clue: Pick out Olympic runners close to victory in stupid remark (6)

indicators.note: the closing letter of VICTORY

blocks.note: to ID is to identify, pick out
the International Olympic Committee runs the Olympics
last letter of VICTORY

annotation.surface: Singling out Olympic athletes near to winning in a foolish comment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Olympic runners' look like athletes; they are the people who run the Games, the IOC.
annotation.definitionFit: A countable sense of the abstract noun: an idiocy is one piece of foolishness, such as a stupid remark.

entries.clue: In court, rate film “superior” (8)

blocks.note: to be up before a judge is to be in court
to mark is to rate or grade
E.T., Spielberg's film

annotation.surface: A courtroom critic rates a film as superior.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film' is the crossword's favourite movie, E.T.
annotation.definitionFit: Upmarket means superior, aimed at the top end of the market.

entries.clue: Man trap set in concrete by day (8)

indicators.note: GIN is placed inside REAL

blocks.note: concrete = real, tangible
a gin is a snare or trap
D = day

annotation.surface: A mantrap is set in concrete during daylight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man trap' reads as one thing; 'Man' is the definition and 'trap' is GIN. 'Concrete' is an adjective, not cement.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: crosswords often use 'man' for any male first name, and Reginald (Reg) is one.

entries.clue: Get down from small trailer perhaps and retreat (6)

blocks.note: S = small
a film trailer is a kind of advertisement, an ad
a den is a private retreat

annotation.surface: Climbing down from a little caravan and heading back inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get down' looks like climbing off; it means to depress, and 'trailer' is a film preview, not a caravan.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to get someone down is informal for making them unhappy, a plain synonym for sadden.
